rubric_items.reason: All eight known REQs (REQ-1..REQ-8) are traced by at least one story; no assumed REQs exist.
S-1, S-2 and S-3 each have one outcome; S-4 bundles two separate constraints (Settings page unchanged and doctor list unchanged).
ACs are Given/When/Then and discriminate (other department's doctors, an Inactive doctor, Inactive entry, 0 count). The singular name boundary is tested only for departments, not specializations.
Counts and names come from the intent, but S-4 uses UI labels (Rename, Deactivate, Activate, Delete, All departments, All specializations) not in the intent and with no cited source.
Clear, consistent terms; front matter and body match; titles are user-facing.

findings.text: S-4 ACs name UI labels (Rename, Deactivate, Activate, Delete, add form, "All departments", "All specializations") that the intent does not contain, and S-4 cites no product-code line for them. REQ-7 says only that the rest is unchanged.

cites.quote: Rest of the Settings page unchanged

findings.suggested_fix: Add a claim that cites the Settings page and doctor list source lines for these labels, or phrase the ACs without naming labels the intent does not give.

findings.text: REQ-6 requires the singular "1 doctor in <name>" for both kinds, but only a department with count 1 is tested. No AC checks a specialization with exactly 1 doctor.

cites.quote: Given a department used by exactly 1 doctor

findings.suggested_fix: Add an S-3 AC: Given a specialization used by exactly 1 doctor, then the accessible name is "1 doctor in <the specialization's name>".

findings.text: S-4 combines two separate constraints, Settings page unchanged (REQ-7) and doctor list unchanged (REQ-8), into one story with two outcomes.

cites.quote: The rest of the Settings page and the doctor list stay as they are

findings.suggested_fix: Split S-4 into one story per constraint, or say why they belong together.
